Summary

The fictional cross-user test returned the owner’s selected private book to the peer. The example reviewer confirmed the intended private-access rule. A separate sharing control observed allowed behavior. Interrupted and unavailable tests remain unassessed.

F-DEMO-01 · Cross-user private book access

Medium · example rating6.5CVSS 3.1 base

An authenticated standard user could retrieve another test user’s selected private book proof. Identity checks, legitimate object reads and subsequent rechecks support this observation. This example concerns confidentiality; it does not establish write or administrator access.

CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N
Evidence: E-01 through E-07 · synthetic observations only

Suggested remediation

Authorize each object read using the authenticated principal and the intended ownership/sharing rule. Test both legitimate and forbidden access after the fix.

Scope and limitations

This sample covers selected HTTP routes and test identities. It does not cover browser sessions, raw scanning, mobile applications or every authorization rule. GET-only work can still have application-side effects. The stopped-state preview does not prove process cleanup or a production Stop deadline.
